comparisonPages.hub.metadata.title: CapRover vs Coolify, Dokploy and Dokku
comparisonPages.hub.metadata.description: Compare CapRover, Coolify, Dokploy and Dokku for Docker hosting on a VPS. Evaluate direct source upload, Compose, Swarm and proxy configuration.
comparisonPages.hub.hero.title: Choose how you want to run Docker apps.
comparisonPages.hub.hero.intro: CapRover is for developers who want to ship from a terminal to a small VPS, manage each app in a dashboard, and edit the NGINX template or Docker service settings directly.
comparisonPages.hub.resourceDescription: CapRover documents a 1 GiB RAM minimum. Coolify lists 2 GB RAM and two CPU cores as its standard baseline and also discusses smaller servers. Dokploy recommends at least 2 GB RAM and 30 GB of disk space.
comparisonPages.hub.shortVersion.title: Compare the workflows you’ll use.

comparisonPages.coolify.metadata.descrip: Compare CapRover’s direct source upload, NGINX templates and Docker Swarm workflow with Coolify’s Git previews, Compose and connected servers.
comparisonPages.coolify.hero.title: Docker Swarm and independent deployment hosts
comparisonPages.coolify.hero.intro: CapRover starts on one VPS and manages apps as Docker Swarm services. Coolify organizes apps, databases and Compose services in project environments and deploys them to servers connected over SSH.
comparisonPages.coolify.hero.verdict: CapRover fits developers who upload code directly from a terminal, manage apps in one Swarm and edit NGINX per app. If your team has formal requirements for separate environments, team roles or independent deployment hosts, check those against the comparison below.
comparisonPages.coolify.resourceDescript: CapRover documents a 1 GiB RAM and 5 GiB disk minimum. Coolify lists 2 GB RAM, two CPU cores and 10 GB free disk as its standard baseline and discusses smaller setups for budget users.

comparisonPages.coolify.articles.0.title: From one VPS to more Swarm workers
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.0.parag: CapRover runs every app as a Swarm service. To add workers, configure a shared push registry and republish existing builds. CapRover can provision that registry or use yours. Stateless replicas can run across workers. Local volumes stay on their original node.
Coolify connects to deployment hosts individually over SSH. Its experimental Swarm integration is deprecated and is reserved for existing Swarm users on v4.
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.1.title: What the deploy command sends
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.1.parag: CapRover’s CLI packages the committed files from a local Git branch and sends them to your VPS. Coolify’s CLI can create an app and trigger deployment of a configured source, such as a Git URL or image. Both can run prebuilt images.
Both can roll back using a retained local image or a registry image where supported. CapRover picks the image from app deployment history. App settings and persistent data stay current.
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.2.title: App templates and proxy middleware
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.2.parag: CapRover generates NGINX routing for an app and lets you edit the full template for settings such as upload limits, response headers, redirects and WebSocket timeouts.

Coolify offers Traefik or Caddy with options such as custom middleware in Traefik. In CapRover, a separate Docker Service Update Override can set a memory limit or a read-only bind mount on the app’s Swarm service.
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.3.title: Compose and environment requirements
comparisonPages.coolify.articles.3.parag: In Coolify, applications and services belong to project environments and deploy to a selected server. The Git-based Compose workflow can also create pull request previews.

CapRover’s experimental importer turns supported Compose fields into dashboard-managed apps. It fits simple stacks with prebuilt images, environment variables and volumes. Compose-defined builds and custom networks are outside the importer’s scope.
Start on a VPS that meets the documented 1 GiB RAM minimum.
Edit the app’s full NGINX template or native Docker service settings.

Provision the cluster’s image registry from the dashboard.
comparisonPages.coolify.choice.competito: Deployments must use a version-controlled Docker Compose file.
One dashboard must manage multiple independent deployment hosts.
The team requires separate project environments, team roles or pull request previews.
comparisonPages.coolify.migrationDescrip: Convert Compose services into CapRover applications or a compatible One-Click template, map domains and environment variables, and migrate persistent data with the database or storage system's own backup tooling.

comparisonPages.dokploy.metadata.descrip: Compare CapRover and Dokploy on Docker Swarm, local source upload, NGINX and Traefik, Compose stacks, registries and rollbacks.
comparisonPages.dokploy.hero.title: Docker Swarm deployment models
comparisonPages.dokploy.hero.intro: CapRover and Dokploy both run applications on Docker Swarm. CapRover manages each app as a Swarm service with its own NGINX template. Dokploy supports individual applications and separate Compose or Stack deployments.
comparisonPages.dokploy.hero.verdict: CapRover fits developers who want direct source uploads and per-app NGINX on a small VPS. If your deployment process requires Compose as the source of truth, permissions per member or separate build servers, check those requirements below.
comparisonPages.dokploy.resourceDescript: CapRover documents a 1 GiB RAM and 5 GiB disk minimum. Dokploy recommends at least 2 GB RAM and 30 GB of disk space.

comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.0.title: Choose the unit you deploy
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.0.parag: In CapRover, create an app and manage its domain, environment, storage and replicas in the same place. Its experimental Compose importer can turn simple image-based services into apps. Compose builds and custom networks need a different deployment path.
Dokploy has a single-service Application workflow too. It also offers Docker Compose and Docker Stack resources for teams that want to keep multiple services under one deployment definition.
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.1.title: Source upload, registry and rollback
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.1.parag: Both have a CLI. CapRover packages committed files from your local Git checkout and uploads them. Dokploy’s documented application deploy command triggers deployment using the application’s configured source.

On a single server, CapRover can roll back from deployment history while the image is available locally or in a registry. To add Swarm workers, configure a registry reachable by every node. CapRover can create that registry, and stateless replicas can then run across workers. Dokploy requires a configured registry to roll back to a specific deployment and also supports Swarm’s automatic rollback. CapRover image rollback leaves app settings and data as they are. Local volumes stay on their node.
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.2.title: NGINX templates and Traefik settings
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.2.parag: CapRover exposes the full NGINX template for each web app. Set an upload limit or response header there. Dokploy uses Traefik and exposes routing and middleware settings for workflows that use Traefik.

Both expose Swarm controls. CapRover accepts a native Docker service override in JSON or YAML, including options such as a read-only bind mount. Dokploy provides dedicated Swarm settings for placement, resources and rollout behavior.
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.3.title: Server, access and backup requirements
comparisonPages.dokploy.articles.3.parag: Dokploy documents separate deployment and build servers, per-member permissions, and scheduled backups for databases and volumes.
CapRover’s open-source project dates to 2017. Its current dashboard adds guided setup, app diagnostics and disk-space alerts while keeping apps on the same Docker Swarm service model.
Start on a VPS that meets the documented 1 GiB RAM minimum.
Edit the full per-app NGINX template and native Docker service settings.
Roll back a retained app image from deployment history on one VPS.
Provision the cluster’s image registry from the dashboard.
Upload committed code directly from a local Git checkout.
comparisonPages.dokploy.choice.competito: Deployments must use Docker Compose or Docker Stack definitions.
The team requires separate member accounts with individual permissions.
Deployment hosts or build servers must be managed independently.
comparisonPages.dokploy.migrationDescrip: Split complex Compose projects into CapRover applications or validate them against the supported One-Click fields. Map domains and environment variables, then transfer persistent data with the database or storage system's own migration tooling.
comparisonPages.dokku.metadata.title: CapRover vs Dokku: Open-Source Dashboard and CLI
comparisonPages.dokku.metadata.descripti: Compare CapRover and Dokku across simplicity, server requirements, open-source dashboards, deployment, Docker orchestration, NGINX, one-click apps and rollback.
comparisonPages.dokku.hero.title: Get a complete open-source dashboard without giving up the command line.
comparisonPages.dokku.hero.intro: CapRover makes the normal path visual and straightforward, while keeping CLI, API, NGINX and Docker controls available when needed. You do not have to choose between ease of use and infrastructure access.
comparisonPages.dokku.hero.verdict: Choose CapRover when dashboard operations, One-Click Apps, rollback and multi-node orchestration should be included in the open-source product. Consider Dokku when a CLI-first workflow, broad builder selection, cron and a composable plugin system are central requirements.
comparisonPages.dokku.resourceDescriptio: Both CapRover and Dokku document a 1 GB minimum with their default Docker-based runtimes. CapRover includes its web dashboard and Docker Swarm model at that published starting requirement.
comparisonPages.dokku.capabilityTitle: Visual operations and CLI deployment in the same open-source product.
comparisonPages.dokku.rows.1.feature: Officially documented minimum of 1 GB RAM
comparisonPages.dokku.rows.2.feature: Purpose-built deployment from a local CLI
comparisonPages.dokku.rows.4.feature: Multi-node orchestration in the standard runtime
comparisonPages.dokku.rows.6.feature: Simple dashboard with an advanced proxy escape hatch
comparisonPages.dokku.rows.7.feature: Simple dashboard with a native orchestrator escape hatch
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.0.title: The dashboard is the simple path
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.0.paragra: Domains, certificates, environment variables, persistent directories, replicas, logs and deployment history are visible and editable without assembling commands.
That makes routine operations approachable for every developer who can access the CapRover dashboard.
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.1.title: The command line is still there
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.1.paragra: Run caprover deploy from a local project, upload an archive, deploy an image or trigger a generic Git webhook. The dashboard itself uses CapRover's HTTP API.
CapRover adds a visual workflow without taking away automation or terminal-based deployment.
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.2.title: Simple does not mean limited
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.2.paragra: Most apps use the generated NGINX and Docker configuration unchanged. Advanced workloads can edit the complete per-app NGINX template and override native Docker service settings.
These controls stay out of the common path until an operator deliberately needs them.
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.3.title: The practical difference
comparisonPages.dokku.articles.3.paragra: Dokku's open-source core is intentionally CLI-first and highly composable through builders, commands and plugins. Dokku Pro adds its official web interface and API separately.
CapRover includes its visual operations workflow, One-Click catalog and Swarm management directly in the open-source platform.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.0: A full web dashboard should be included in the open-source platform.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.1: You want a simple visual workflow and direct local deployment together.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.2: You want deep NGINX and Docker controls available without making them the default workflow.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.3: Docker Swarm clustering and rollback should be managed through the same product.
comparisonPages.dokku.choice.caprover.4: You rely on a one-click catalog of deployable applications and databases.
SSH commands and Git push should be the primary interface.
Buildpacks and a composable plugin system are essential.
You need built-in cron task definitions or global environment variables.
comparisonPages.dokku.migrationDescripti: Convert Dokku configuration into CapRover environment variables and application settings, add captain-definition files, map domains, and migrate datastore contents with the database's own backup and restore tools.
